section_summary: This section documents diplomatic and consular issues arising from strict foreign exchange control regulations enacted in the Kwantung Leased Territory in 1940 and 1941. It covers the refusal of the American Consul at Dairen to accept local currency for a consular bill of health for the Japanese vessel San Pedro Maru because exchange regulations blocked remitting official funds without petitioning the Japanese Ambassador to Manchukuo. The State Department and the American Embassy in Tokyo protested Japanese exchange restrictions on official American funds and clarified the legal status of the Kwantung Leased Territory, maintaining that Dairen was not an integral part of the Japanese Empire. Later correspondence addresses procedures for the Dairen Consulate to receive funds remitted through the Yokohama Specie Bank under local regulations.

subfiles.about: Transmits and explains the revised foreign exchange control regulations of the Kwantung Leased Territory promulgated on July 11, 1940.
subfiles.from: L. H. Gourley, American Consul, Dairen
subfiles.summary: American Consul L. H. Gourley transmits an English translation of the Kwantung Province foreign exchange regulations as revised on July 11, 1940. The revision drastically reduces the currency travelers can carry without a permit from 500 to 50 yen, requires special permits for foreign remittances, and restricts foreign exchange transactions to authorized banks. The enclosed full translation details comprehensive controls on gold, foreign securities, exchange contracts, and external business assets administered by Japanese authorities.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 31: Kwantung Leased Territory Foreign Exchange Regulations Become More Strict

subfiles.about: Reports that the Consul at Dairen refused local currency for a bill of health for the San Pedro Maru due to exchange restrictions on official funds.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that the San Pedro Maru sailed from Dairen without a consular bill of health after the Consul refused local currency pending exchange control rulings. Grew also presented an oral statement to the Japanese Foreign Minister regarding official remittances.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 322 from Tokyo regarding Refusal of Bill of Health for San Pedro Maru

subfiles.about: Requests further information on the exchange situation at Dairen following the refusal of a bill of health to the San Pedro Maru.
subfiles.summary: The State Department requests immediate information on whether the Dairen Consul's refusal of fees in local currency constitutes a general policy or a test case.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 193 to Tokyo regarding Bill of Health Refusal at Dairen

subfiles.about: Reviews consular fee regulations concerning the collection and exchange of foreign currency for consular services.
subfiles.from: Thomas Burke, Chief, Division of International Communications
subfiles.summary: Thomas Burke notes that Foreign Service regulations require consular fees collected in foreign currency to cover the full exchange value for purchase of sight drafts.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Collection of Consular Fees in Foreign Currency

subfiles.about: Reports representations made to the Japanese Foreign Minister regarding Dairen exchange authorities requiring permits for official remittances.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits a memorandum of conversation and an oral statement presented to Foreign Minister Matsuoka protesting the Dairen authorities' refusal to exempt official American remittances from exchange control and their demand that applications be addressed to the Japanese Ambassador to Manchukuo.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5401: Difficulties of the American Consulate at Dairen with the Exchange Control Authorities

subfiles.about: Analyzes the circumstances under which the San Pedro Maru departed Dairen without a bill of health and recommends levying a fine.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Adams, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Walter A. Adams reviews the San Pedro Maru incident, agreeing the Consul was justified in suspending services but arguing the shipmaster acted improperly by ignoring American law, recommending a reasonable fine be imposed.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Departure of the San Pedro Maru from Dairen
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations

subfiles.about: Provides a detailed account of the exchange controversy at Dairen, the San Pedro Maru incident, and the provisional resumption of consular services.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew provides comprehensive details on the exchange controversy at Dairen, explaining that the dispute arose when the Consulate attempted to purchase a small draft to reimburse the Zurich Consulate. The Consul suspended services rather than petition the Japanese Ambassador to Manchukuo, maintaining that Dairen fell under Japanese Empire assurances. Following representations in Tokyo, Dairen exchange authorities granted provisional permission to purchase exchange without application, allowing normal consular operations to resume.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 471 from Tokyo regarding Settlement of Dairen Consular Exchange Difficulties

subfiles.about: Examines historical treaties and legal precedents to refute the assertion that Dairen is an integral part of the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Adams, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Adams examines the 1898 and 1905 treaties, a 1900 Solicitor opinion, and legal literature to demonstrate that China retained sovereignty over Kwantung and that the United States has never regarded Dairen as an integral part of Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Legal Status of the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations

subfiles.about: Instructs the Embassy to inform the Dairen Consul that the United States does not consider Dairen an integral part of the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.summary: The Department instructs the Embassy to correct the Dairen Consul's statement describing Dairen as an integral part of the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 215 to Tokyo regarding Legal Status of Dairen

subfiles.about: Transmits a confidential memorandum regarding Japanese jurisdiction in the Kwantung Leased Territory to the American Ambassador in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal slip enclosing the April 2 memorandum regarding Japanese jurisdiction in the Kwantung Leased Territory for the American Ambassador.
subfiles.title: Instruction Transmitting Memorandum on Japanese Jurisdiction in Kwantung Leased Territory

subfiles.about: Comments on Embassy Tokyo's explanation of the Consul's wording regarding Dairen's relationship to the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Cabot Coville notes the drafting error in Tokyo's telegram, observing that saying Dairen is 'in' Japan is objectionable but requires no further action.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Tokyo's Despatch No. 5507 on Dairen Terminology
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations

subfiles.about: Clarifies an Embassy drafting error concerning the Dairen Consul's statement on the legal status of Dairen.
subfiles.from: George A. Makinson, First Secretary of Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: First Secretary Makinson explains that the Embassy mistakenly reported the Consul called Dairen an 'integral part' of Japan, when he actually stated Dairen was 'in' Japan, and confirms forwarding Department instructions to Dairen.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5507: Difficulties of the American Consulate at Dairen with the Exchange Control Authorities

subfiles.about: Reports that the Yokohama Specie Bank requires the Dairen Consulate to apply to the Japanese Ambassador to Manchukuo to receive remitted funds.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew requests instructions after the Yokohama Specie Bank required the Dairen Consulate to submit an application addressed to the Ambassador to Manchukuo.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1374 from Tokyo regarding Application to Japanese Ambassador to Manchukuo

subfiles.about: Provides legal comment on addressing the Japanese representative at Hsinking rather than to Manchukuo.
subfiles.from: Richard W. Flournoy, Assistant Legal Adviser
subfiles.summary: Flournoy notes that 'Japanese Ambassador at Hsinking' is legally equivalent to 'Japanese Ambassador to Manchukuo'.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Addressing the Japanese Ambassador at Hsinking

subfiles.about: Authorizes the Dairen Consul to apply for remittance funds as required by local regulations, suggesting alternate phrasing if possible.
subfiles.summary: Secretary Hull authorizes the Consul at Dairen to apply for remittance funds, suggesting he substitute 'Ambassador at Hsinking' if possible.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 513 to Tokyo regarding Application for Remittance at Dairen
